construction_markdown:
Work over `F_256 = F_2[ζ]/(ζ^8+ζ^4+ζ^3+ζ+1)`, with the coefficient-basis ordering. Its unique subfield of order 16 defines the completed Garcia–Stichtenoth tower. Intermediate fields are fixed fields of the lexicographically ordered translation subgroups of `F_16`; splitting places, functions, and Riemann–Roch bases are ordered lexicographically in the induced tower presentation.

Main flag: at GS level `(k,s)=(4,3)`, use `L_1=8,355,840` splitting rational places and the pole `P_∞`. Put `a_0=1,015,808`, `a_1=1,037,243`, and `t=a_1-a_0=21,435`. From the genus bound `g≤554,753`, deterministically choose `F_256`-subspaces

`U_0 ⊂ L(a_0P_∞) ⊂ L(a_1P_∞)`,

with dimensions `461,056` and `482,491`, respectively, by taking the lexicographically first independent functions and extending the first basis. Concatenate their evaluations with `RM(1,7)=[128,8,64]_2`. The complement `U_1/U_0` has `F_256`-dimension `t`.

Auxiliary code: at GS level `(3,2)`, take the first `L_2=209,715` of the guaranteed `261,120` splitting places and divisor `H=38,231Q_∞`. Choose the lexicographically first `t=21,435` independent functions in `L(H)`.

Concatenate this auxiliary AG code with the explicit binary code `J=[I_8|P]`, where the twelve-bit rows of `P` are

`101011100011, 110010001111, 100111010101, 101101111000, 010110111100, 001011011110, 000101101111, 111100100101`.

The 256 row sums of this matrix have weight enumerator `1+130z^8+120z^12+5z^16`; hence `J=[20,8,8]_2`. The auxiliary concatenation has length `4,194,300`; append four zero coordinates.

For `f=f_0+Σu_iw_i∈U_1`, output its main RM-concatenated evaluation followed by the auxiliary encoding of `(u_1,…,u_t)`. All field identifications use the fixed coefficient basis, and all coordinate orders are lexicographic.
distance_audit: For quotient zero, `f∈U_0\{0}` and the main weight is at least `(8,355,840−1,015,808)·64 = 7,340,032·64 = 469,762,048`.
For quotient nonzero, the main weight is at least `(8,355,840−1,037,243)·64 = 7,318,597·64 = 468,390,208`.
A nonzero auxiliary word has weight at least `(209,715−38,231)·8 = 171,484·8 = 1,371,872`.
Thus the nonzero-quotient case has weight at least `468,390,208+1,371,872=469,762,080`, exceeding the target by 32.
Both independent internal audits reproduced the tower, inner-code, length, dimension, and two-case distance arithmetic.
explicitness_audit: The field is given by a specific irreducible polynomial and coefficient basis.
The completed tower is specified by `z_{i+1}^16+z_{i+1}=x_i^17`, with deterministic intermediate fixed fields.
Evaluation places are selected from the explicit splitting places in coefficient-lexicographic order.
The nested Riemann–Roch spaces, complement, and auxiliary message space use deterministic greedy bases in canonical function-field normal forms.
Both inner encoders are explicit: affine-function evaluation for `RM(1,7)` and the displayed systematic matrix for `J`.
The only final padding is exactly four zero coordinates; no random or searched constituent is used.

To cross `7/1920` within this Construction-X architecture, seek an explicit auxiliary `[2^22,≥226,240,≥1,809,920]_2` code, corresponding to `t≥28,280`.
obstructions: The rate `482,491/134,217,728≈0.0035948380827903748` is strictly below `7/1920`; crossing requires dimension at least `3,914,684`, another 54,756 dimensions.

For a one-level inner `[b,m,e]_2`, the GS envelope is `(m/b)(1−7b/(16e)−1/(2^(m/2)−1))_+`. Exact dimension-eight code bounds eliminate all apparent improvements over `[128,8,64]`; thus merely replacing RM by another eight-dimensional inner cannot cross the ceiling.
The auxiliary construction is a genuine generalized-concatenation mechanism, but its present parameters close only part of the finite gap.
proof_markdown:
## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with parameters

`[1,073,741,824, 3,859,928, ≥469,762,048]_2`.

## Tower data

Use the completed GS tower over `F_256` with `q=16`, `p=2`, and `r=4`. Formula (3) gives

`g_5=16^5+16^4−16^3−2·16^2+1=1,109,505`,

so Proposition 2.1 gives `g_(4,3)≤floor(g_5/2+1)=554,753` and at least

`(16^2−1)16^3·2^3=8,355,840`

splitting rational places.

For the auxiliary level, the even-level formula gives

`g_4=16^4+16^3−16^3/2−3·16^2/2−16+1=67,185`.

Hence `g_(3,2)≤floor(g_4/4+1)=16,797`, while the number of splitting rational places is at least

`(16^2−1)16^2·2^2=261,120`.

## Inner-code lemma

Let `J=[I_8|P]` with the displayed twelve-bit rows. Its rank is eight. Applying the recurrence `S_0={0}`, `S_i=S_(i−1)∪(S_(i−1)+row_i)` and counting weights after the eighth row gives

`W_J(z)=1+130z^8+120z^12+5z^16`.

This is an exhaustive enumeration of 256 explicitly specified vectors, so `J=[20,8,8]_2`. The other inner code is the affine-function code on `F_2^7`: every nonconstant affine function has weight 64 and the nonzero constant has weight 128. Thus it is `[128,8,64]_2`.

## Main nested codes

Set `a_0=1,015,808` and `a_1=1,037,243`. Riemann–Roch gives

`ell(a_0P_∞)≥a_0+1−554,753=461,056`,

`ell(a_1P_∞)≥a_1+1−554,753=482,491`.

Choose deterministic nested subspaces `U_0⊂U_1` of exactly these dimensions. Their complement has dimension

`t=482,491−461,056=21,435`

over `F_256`. Evaluation is injective because `a_1<L_1`. After RM concatenation, the resulting nested binary codes `A_0⊂A_1` have dimensions `8·461,056` and `8·482,491`, with

`d(A_0)≥64(L_1−a_0)=469,762,048`,

`d(A_1)≥64(L_1−a_1)=468,390,208`.

## Auxiliary code

At level `(3,2)`, select `L_2=209,715` splitting places and put `H=38,231Q_∞`. Then

`ell(H)≥38,231+1−16,797=21,435=t`,

and its evaluation code has distance at least

`209,715−38,231=171,484`.

Take a deterministic `t`-dimensional subspace and concatenate it with `J`. This gives a binary code `B'` of dimension `8t=171,480`, length `209,715·20=4,194,300`, and distance at least

`171,484·8=1,371,872`.

Appending four zeros gives `B⊂F_2^(2^22)` with the same dimension and distance.

## Construction-X step

Fix the basis complement `U_1=U_0⊕W` and identify `W` with the auxiliary message space. For `f=f_0+w∈U_1`, define

`Enc(f)=(Enc_main(f), Enc_B(w))`.

This map is binary linear. Its main component is injective, so the final dimension is exactly

`8·482,491=3,859,928`.

If `w=0` and `f≠0`, the word lies in `A_0` and has weight at least `469,762,048`. If `w≠0`, its main part has weight at least `468,390,208` and its auxiliary part has weight at least `1,371,872`; hence its total weight is at least

`468,390,208+1,371,872=469,762,080`.

Thus every nonzero word meets the required distance.

Finally,

`8,355,840·128 + 209,715·20 + 4`

`=1,069,547,520+4,194,300+4`

`=1,073,741,824=2^30`.

This proves the theorem.

proof_steps.proof: Apply the completed-tower genus and splitting-place bounds with `(q,p,r)=(16,2,4)`; the displayed integer arithmetic gives the two required levels.
proof_steps.statement: The main and auxiliary GS steps have the claimed genus and rational-place bounds.

proof_steps.proof: `I_8` proves rank eight; exhaustive XOR enumeration of the 256 row sums gives weights only 0, 8, 12, and 16 with enumerator `1+130z^8+120z^12+5z^16`.
proof_steps.statement: The displayed matrix generates an explicit `[20,8,8]_2` code.

proof_steps.proof: Riemann–Roch supplies dimensions 461,056 and 482,491; deterministic greedy bases produce an exact nested flag. AG evaluation and RM concatenation give the two main distances.
proof_steps.statement: There are nested main codes `A_0⊂A_1` with quotient dimension 171,480 and distances 469,762,048 and 468,390,208.

proof_steps.proof: The auxiliary divisor gives `[209,715,21,435,≥171,484]_(256)`; concatenation with `J` and four zero pads gives `[2^22,171,480,≥1,371,872]_2`.
proof_steps.statement: The auxiliary code has exactly the dimension needed to encode `A_1/A_0`.

proof_steps.proof: The quotient-zero case uses `d(A_0)`; the quotient-nonzero case uses `d(A_1)+d(B)=469,762,080`. Injectivity of the main encoder gives the exact dimension, and the two coordinate portions sum to `2^30`.
Substituting the Griesmer bound into the one-level objective leaves five hypothetical dimension-eight parameter triples; the exact dimension-eight minimum-length classification excludes all five.
proof_steps.statement: No dimension-eight binary inner code beats `7/1920` in the ordinary one-level GS calculation.

research_direction: Use a nested GS divisor flag and encode its quotient in the former zero-padding coordinates via a second GS code with an explicit `[20,8,8]` binary inner code. This is Construction X rather than one-level parameter tuning, but the proved finite instance remains below the template ceiling.
theorem_statement: There exists a deterministic binary linear code `C⊂F_2^1,073,741,824` with dimension `3,859,928` and minimum distance at least `469,762,048`.
title: Nested GS Construction X with an explicit [20,8,8] side inner code
